faq_section.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq_section.description: These are some of the most common doubts before starting a job with me. The idea is for you to have clarity, confidence, and realistic expectations.

items.q: Do you work as a freelance or as a company?
items.a: I work as a professional freelancer. This allows me to be directly involved in each project, without intermediaries or delegations. You speak directly with me throughout the process.

items.q: Why are your services not the cheapest?
items.a: Because I don't offer generic solutions or automated work. My approach is preventive, technical, and responsible. I invest real time in analyzing, proposing, and executing correctly.

items.q: How do I know you won't disappear mid-project?
items.a: I work with a limited number of projects at the same time and maintain clear communication from the start. I don't overcharge my schedule or delegate your project to third parties.

items.q: What kind of clients do you work with?
items.a: I work with people and companies that value stability, security, and work well done. I do not accept projects where only 'the cheapest' is sought.

items.q: Do you need access to my website?
items.a: For audits and technical work, yes. Access is necessary to review the actual state of the site. Everything is handled with confidentiality and best practices.

items.q: Do you work only with WordPress?
items.a: My main specialty is WordPress, but I also work with modern technologies and custom development when the project requires it.

items.q: Do you offer support after the job?
items.a: Yes. Depending on the service, I offer guidance, maintenance, or ongoing support. I don't deliver a project and disappear.

items.q: Do you work with clients outside of Colombia?
items.a: Yes. I work remotely with clients in different countries. Communication is adapted to the agreed medium and time.

items.q: How long does an audit or intervention take?
items.a: It depends on the state and size of the site. Before starting, I explain the scope, estimated times, and next steps so there are no surprises.

items.q: What if my problem can't be solved?
items.a: I am honest from the beginning. If something is not viable or not worth doing, I say it clearly. I prefer transparency over unrealistic promises.
